docs.title: Terror Fibercraft 1000x Toolkit
docs.text: The Terror Fibercraft 1000x admin cluster toolkit manages the biggest Xbox / Windows Store ARK: Survival Evolved (ASE) crossplay cluster on Nitrado. This documentation covers the installable Python package.

docs.title: What's inside
docs.text:
• RCON client — Source RCON protocol, both sync and asyncio.
  • Nitrado REST client — async control of Nitrado custom game servers.
  • Sculpt generator — build cheat spawnactor admin-terrain batches.
  • Settings — pydantic-validated configuration from env vars / config.json.
  • Discord bot — slash commands wrapping the above, cog-based.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
uv sync --extra bot          # dev groups + Discord extra
uv run tf-generator list     # see the sculpt API
tf-discord-bot --config config.json

See Usage for the full manual and API Reference for the package documentation.

docs.title: Safety note
docs.text: Admin sculpt tools are admin terrain only. Players who use them to box bases or block paths are banned. See the Code of Conduct in the parent repo.

docs.title: Terror Fibercraft 1000x — Usage Guide (v3.1)
docs.text: The toolkit is a proper, installable Python package under src/terrorfibercraft/, managed natively with uv. This page is the canonical reference for installing and running every tool.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11+ and uv (recommended) or plain pip.

uv sync --extra bot   # installs the package + dev groups + Discord extra
# to also pre-build docs tooling:  uv sync --all-groups --extra bot

uv sync creates a .venv, installs the package, and installs the dev dependency group (which itself pulls in the lint, test, and docs groups) from the committed uv.lock. The bot extra adds discord.py, needed only if you run the Discord bot. Activate the venv, or prefix commands with uv run.

The full set of dependency groups:

Group Contents lint ruff, mypy test pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, tox, tox-uv docs mkdocs, mkdocs-material, mkdocstrings[python], mkdocs-autorefs dev pre-commit, build, twine + includes lint/test/docs

Or, with plain pip:

pip install -e ".[bot]"        # runtime + Discord
pip install -e ".[bot]" --config-settings=...  # extras not grouped here

docs.title: Environment / secrets
docs.text:
Never commit real tokens. Two supported sources:

  1. config.json (for the Discord bot only) — copy config.example.json → config.json.
  2. Environment variables — copy .env.example → .env, or set real env vars.
Var Purpose TF_DISCORD_TOKEN Discord bot token TF_NITRADO_TOKEN Nitrado REST API token TF_ADMIN_ROLE Required Discord role for admin commands (default Admin) TF_LOG_LEVEL Logging level (default INFO)

docs.title: Console scripts
docs.text:
All tools ship as console scripts (installed into .venv/bin or Scripts).

Script What it does tf-generator Build / convert / batch / apply cheat spawnactor sculpt batches tf-ark-rcon RCON protocol selftest & diagnostics tf-nitrado List Nitrado services / test the REST API tf-discord-bot Run the Discord admin bot

Each is also runnable as a module, e.g. python -m terrorfibercraft.scripts.generator_cli ....

docs.text:
tf-generator gen --preset dino_gate
tf-generator gen --mode box --cols 9 --rows 6 --depth 9 --hole behemoth --floor --ceiling --blueprint watervein --json
tf-generator convert --map ragnarok --lat 30.2 --lon 32.8
tf-generator batch --file spots.json > walls.txt
tf-generator list

docs.title: Discord bot
docs.text:
cp config.example.json config.json   # then fill in tokens
tf-discord-bot --config config.json

The bot registers slash commands via the AdminCog (scripts/cog.py): /status, /players, /donate, /restart. Admin-only commands require the role named by admin_role.

docs.title: Lint, type-check, test, build
docs.text:
Via uv directly:

uv run ruff check src tests
uv run ruff format --check src tests
uv run mypy src
uv run pytest
uv build

Or via the tox matrix (lint, docs, build, and py311/py312/py313):

uv run tox -e lint        # ruff + format-check + mypy
uv run tox -e py312       # pytest on Python 3.12
uv run tox -e docs        # mkdocs build --strict
uv run tox -e build       # uv build + twine check
uv run tox                # whole matrix

pre-commit is configured (.pre-commit-config.yaml):

uv run pre-commit install

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
The API reference is generated from docstrings with MkDocs + mkdocstrings:

uv run mkdocs serve       # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
uv run mkdocs build --strict

Source lives in docs/; the generated site is written to site/ (gitignored).

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
A Dockerfile runs the Discord bot in a container. Mount your config.json (or set TF_* env vars) and run:

docker build -t terrorfibercraft .
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/config.json:/app/config.json" terrorfibercraft

docs.title: CI
docs.text: .github/workflows/ci.yml lints, formats, type-checks, and tests on Python 3.11–3.13, builds sdist + wheel, validates them with twine, and publishes to PyPI (trusted OIDC) on v* tags. A Dockerfile job builds/pushes a ghcr.io image on main. .github/dependabot.yml keeps pip (grouped) and GitHub Actions + docker base images updated.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseSettings

Top-level application settings.

Example config.json: { "discord_token": "...", "nitrado_token": "...", "admin_role": "Admin", "donate_message": "...", "servers": { "island": {...} } }

Source code in src\terrorfibercraft\config.py 
class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """Top-level application settings.

    Example config.json:
    {
      "discord_token": "...",
      "nitrado_token": "...",
      "admin_role": "Admin",
      "donate_message": "...",
      "servers": { "island": {...} }
    }
    """

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="TF_", env_file=".env", extra="ignore")

    discord_token: SecretStr | None = None
    nitrado_token: SecretStr | None = None
    admin_role: str = "Admin"
    donate_message: str = "Support the cluster: <donation link>"
    servers: dict[str, ServerConfig] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    log_level: str = "INFO"

    @classmethod
    def from_file(cls, path: str | Path) -> Settings:
        """Load settings from a JSON file, merging environment overrides."""
        raw: dict[str, Any] = {}
        p = Path(path)
        if p.exists():
            import json

            raw = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return cls(**raw)

class AdminCog(app_commands.Group):
    """Typed facade so mypy can validate usage without discord internals."""

    def __init__(self, settings: Settings) -> None:
        self._group = _AdminCog(settings)

    def attach(self, tree: app_commands.CommandTree) -> None:
        tree.add_command(self._group)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._group._close()

docs.title: Discord
docs.text:
Terror Fibercraft 1000x admin Discord bot (ASE / Nitrado CrossPlay).

Because Arkon does NOT support ASE on Nitrado, this bot is the primary Discord integration. It wraps the async :class:~terrorfibercraft.nitrado.NitradoClient and :class:~terrorfibercraft.rcon.AsyncRconClient behind the /admin slash commands defined in :mod:terrorfibercraft.scripts.cog.

Configuration is loaded via :class:terrorfibercraft.config.Settings from config.json (default) or the TF_ environment variables.

Run

python -m terrorfibercraft.scripts.discord_bot [--config path/to/config.json]

docs.title: TerrorBot
docs.text:
Bases: Client

Application-command Discord bot for cluster administration.

Source code in src\terrorfibercraft\scripts\discord_bot.py 
class TerrorBot(discord.Client):
    """Application-command Discord bot for cluster administration."""

    def __init__(self, settings: Settings) -> None:
        intents = discord.Intents.default()
        super().__init__(intents=intents)
        self.settings = settings
        self.tree = discord.app_commands.CommandTree(self)
        self.cog = AdminCog(settings)
        self.cog.attach(self.tree)

    async def on_ready(self) -> None:
        await self.tree.sync()
        logger.info("TerrorFibercraft bot logged in as %s", self.user)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self.cog.close()
        await super().close()

docs.title: Generators
docs.text:
Admin custom-cave / sculpt generator for Terror Fibercraft 1000x.

Produces ordered cheat spawnactor command batches that drop terminal structures to sculpt admin terrain: cave walls, sealed base shells, floating platforms, canyon chokes, and cliff-hollow rat holes.

ADMIN terrain only. Players using these to box bases or block paths is a bannable exploit.

docs.text:
build_commands(options)

Generate a sculting batch from :class:GenOptions.

Source code in src\terrorfibercraft\generator.py 
def build_commands(options: GenOptions) -> SculptResult:
    """Generate a sculting batch from :class:`GenOptions`."""
    if options.preset:
        if options.preset not in PRESETS:
            raise GeneratorError(f"Unknown preset '{options.preset}'. Choices: {', '.join(PRESETS)}")
        for k, v in PRESETS[options.preset].items():
            setattr(options, k, v)

    bp = resolve_blueprint(options.blueprint)
    if options.mode not in ("wall", "floor", "platform", "box"):
        raise GeneratorError("mode must be wall|floor|platform|box")

    lines: list[str] = []
    meta: dict[str, object] = {
        "mode": options.mode,
        "blueprint": options.blueprint,
        "spacing": options.spacing,
        "preset": options.preset,
    }

    if options.mode == "wall":
        lines += _emit_wall(
            bp,
            options.cols,
            options.rows,
            options.spacing,
            options.forward,
            options.zstart,
            options.hole,
            "WALL",
        )
        meta.update(cols=options.cols, rows=options.rows, hole=options.hole)
    elif options.mode in ("floor", "platform"):
        lines += _emit_platform(
            bp,
            options.depth,
            options.cols,
            options.spacing,
            options.forward,
            options.zstart,
            "PLATFORM/FLOOR",
        )
        meta.update(depth=options.depth, cols=options.cols)
    elif options.mode == "box":
        lines.append("# BOX SHELL — run each wall while facing that side.")
        for side in ("NORTH (in front)", "EAST (in front)", "SOUTH (in front)", "WEST (in front)"):
            lines += _emit_wall(
                bp,
                options.cols,
                options.rows,
                options.spacing,
                options.forward,
                options.zstart,
                options.hole,
                f"BOX WALL — {side}",
            )
        if options.floor:
            lines += _emit_platform(
                bp,
                options.depth,
                options.cols,
                options.spacing,
                options.forward,
                options.zstart,
                "BOX FLOOR (under you)",
            )
        if options.ceiling:
            lines += _emit_platform(
                bp,
                options.depth,
                options.cols,
                options.spacing,
                options.forward,
                options.zstart + options.rows * options.spacing,
                "BOX CEILING",
            )
        meta.update(
            cols=options.cols,
            rows=options.rows,
            hole=options.hole,
            depth=options.depth,
            floor=options.floor,
            ceiling=options.ceiling,
        )

    return SculptResult(lines, meta)

Convert ARK lat/lon to a setplayerpos command.

Source code in src\terrorfibercraft\generator.py 
def convert_coords(map_name: str, lat: float, lon: float, z: float = 0.0) -> str:
    """Convert ARK lat/lon to a ``setplayerpos`` command."""
    if map_name not in MAP_TRANSFORMS:
        raise GeneratorError(f"map must be one of: {', '.join(MAP_TRANSFORMS)}")
    slat, slon, mlat, mlon, approx = MAP_TRANSFORMS[map_name]
    x = (lon - slon) * mlon
    y = (lat - slat) * mlat
    flag = "  # APPROXIMATE — verify with arkids.net for this map" if approx else ""
    return f"# {map_name}: Lat {lat}, Lon {lon}{flag}\ncheat setplayerpos {x:.0f} {y:.0f} {z:.0f}"

docs.title: NitradoClient
docs.text:
An asyncio-friendly wrapper around the Nitrado REST API.

Uses :mod:httpx behind the scenes and exposes small, typed methods for the operations the toolkit needs. Requires a Nitrado API token.

Source code in src\terrorfibercraft\nitrado.py 
class NitradoClient:
    """An asyncio-friendly wrapper around the Nitrado REST API.

    Uses :mod:`httpx` behind the scenes and exposes small, typed methods for
    the operations the toolkit needs. Requires a Nitrado API token.
    """

    def __init__(self, token: str, base: str = API_BASE, timeout: float = 20.0):
        if not token:
            raise ValueError("Nitrado API token is required")
        self._token = token
        self._base = base.rstrip("/")
        self._client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None
        self._timeout = timeout

    @property
    def _http(self) -> httpx.AsyncClient:
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
                base_url=self._base,
                timeout=self._timeout,
                headers={
                    "Authorization": f"Bearer {self._token}",
                    "Accept": "application/json",
                },
            )
        return self._client

    async def _request(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        data: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        r = await self._http.request(method, path, data=data)
        if r.status_code in (401, 403):
            raise NitradoAuthError(f"{r.status_code} on {method} {path}")
        if r.status_code == 404:
            raise NitradoNotFoundError(f"{r.status_code} on {method} {path}")
        r.raise_for_status()
        try:
            payload = r.json()
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return {"raw": r.text}
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise NitradoError(f"Unexpected JSON shape from {method} {path}")
        return dict(payload)

    async def list_services(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
        r = await self._request("GET", "/services")
        data = r.get("data") or {}
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            services = data.get("services")
            if isinstance(services, list):
                return [dict(s) for s in services if isinstance(s, dict)]
        services = r.get("services")
        if isinstance(services, list):
            return [dict(s) for s in services if isinstance(s, dict)]
        return []

    async def gameserver(self, service_id: int | str, gs_id: int | str) -> dict[str, object]:
        r = await self._request("GET", f"/services/{service_id}/gameservers/{gs_id}")
        data = r.get("data")
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            gs = data.get("gameserver")
            if isinstance(gs, dict):
                return dict(gs)
        return r

    async def restart(
        self, service_id: int | str, gs_id: int | str, message: str = "Admin restart"
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        return await self._request(
            "POST",
            f"/services/{service_id}/gameservers/{gs_id}/restart",
            data={"message": message},
        )

    async def stop(self, service_id: int | str, gs_id: int | str) -> dict[str, object]:
        return await self._request("POST", f"/services/{service_id}/gameservers/{gs_id}/stop")

    async def start(self, service_id: int | str, gs_id: int | str) -> dict[str, object]:
        return await self._request("POST", f"/services/{service_id}/gameservers/{gs_id}/start")

    async def get_settings(self, service_id: int | str, gs_id: int | str) -> dict[str, object]:
        return await self._request("GET", f"/services/{service_id}/gameservers/{gs_id}/settings")

    async def update_config(
        self,
        service_id: int | str,
        gs_id: int | str,
        game_ini: str | None = None,
        gameusersettings_ini: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Push ARK config file contents.

        Field names follow Nitrado's documented settings schema. Verify the
        exact field keys against the current Nitrado developer portal.
        """
        form: dict[str, str] = {}
        if game_ini is not None:
            form["settings[game.ini]"] = game_ini
        if gameusersettings_ini is not None:
            form["settings[gameusersettings.ini]"] = gameusersettings_ini
        if not form:
            raise NitradoError("No config provided to update_config")
        return await self._request(
            "POST",
            f"/services/{service_id}/gameservers/{gs_id}/settings",
            data=form,
        )

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        if self._client is not None:
            await self._client.aclose()
            self._client = None

async def update_config(
    self,
    service_id: int | str,
    gs_id: int | str,
    game_ini: str | None = None,
    gameusersettings_ini: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Push ARK config file contents.

    Field names follow Nitrado's documented settings schema. Verify the
    exact field keys against the current Nitrado developer portal.
    """
    form: dict[str, str] = {}
    if game_ini is not None:
        form["settings[game.ini]"] = game_ini
    if gameusersettings_ini is not None:
        form["settings[gameusersettings.ini]"] = gameusersettings_ini
    if not form:
        raise NitradoError("No config provided to update_config")
    return await self._request(
        "POST",
        f"/services/{service_id}/gameservers/{gs_id}/settings",

docs.title: RCON
docs.text:
Source RCON protocol client for ARK (ASE/ASA) servers.

Implements the Valve Source RCON wire protocol over TCP. Commands are framed as little-endian packets: length(4) | id(4) | type(4) | body | null | null.

Both a synchronous, dependency-free client (RconClient) and an asyncio client (AsyncRconClient) are provided.

docs.text:
Synchronous, dependency-free RCON client.

Example

with RconClient("111.111.111.111", 27020, "rconpass") as r: r.send_many(["listplayers", "gamestat"])

Usage as a context manager is recommended so the socket is always closed.

class RconClient:
    """Synchronous, dependency-free RCON client.

    Example:
        with RconClient("111.111.111.111", 27020, "rconpass") as r:
            r.send_many(["listplayers", "gamestat"])

    Usage as a context manager is recommended so the socket is always closed.
    """

    def __init__(self, host: str, port: int, password: str, timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT):
        if not host:
            raise ValueError("host is required")
        self.host = host
        self.port = int(port)
        self.password = password
        self.timeout = timeout
        self._sock: socket.socket | None = None
        self._id = 0

    def connect(self) -> None:
        self._sock = socket.create_connection((self.host, self.port), timeout=self.timeout)
        self._id = 1
        self._auth()

    def _auth(self) -> None:
        if self._sock is None:
            raise RconError("not connected")
        self._sock.sendall(_encode(self._id, SERVERDATA_AUTH, self.password))
        pkt, _ = self._read_packet()
        if pkt.request_id == -1:
            raise RconAuthError("RCON auth failed (bad password?)")
        # drain trailing packet
        self._sock.settimeout(0.5)
        try:
            self._drain()
        finally:
            self._sock.settimeout(self.timeout)

    def send(self, command: str) -> str:
        """Send a single command and return its concatenated response body."""
        if self._sock is None:
            self.connect()
        assert self._sock is not None
        self._id += 1
        myid = self._id
        self._sock.sendall(_encode(myid, SERVERDATA_EXECCOMMAND, command))
        out: list[bytes] = []
        while True:
            pkt, _ = self._read_packet()
            if pkt.ptype == SERVERDATA_RESPONSE and not pkt.body:
                break
            if pkt.body:
                out.append(pkt.body)
        return b"".join(out).decode("utf-8", "replace")

    def send_many(self, commands: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:
        """Send multiple commands sequentially, returning each response."""
        return [self.send(c.strip()) for c in commands if c.strip()]

    def _read_packet(self) -> tuple[RCONResponse, int]:
        if self._sock is None:
            raise RconError("not connected")
        head = _recv_exact(self._sock, 4)
        if len(head) < 4:
            raise RconError("connection closed while reading header")
        size = struct.unpack("<i", head)[0]
        if size < 0 or size > 4096 * 16:
            raise RconError(f"invalid packet size: {size}")
        data = _recv_exact(self._sock, size)
        if len(data) < size:
            raise RconError("connection closed mid-packet")
        pkt_id, ptype, body = _decode_header(head + data)
        return RCONResponse(pkt_id, ptype, bytes(body)), size

    def _drain(self) -> None:
        if self._sock is None:
            return
        prev = self._sock.gettimeout()
        try:
            self._sock.settimeout(0.3)
            while True:
                try:
                    self._read_packet()
                except Exception:
                    break
        finally:
            self._sock.settimeout(prev)

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._sock is not None:
            try:
                self._sock.close()
            finally:
                self._sock = None

    def __enter__(self) -> RconClient:
        self.connect()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
        self.close()

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[str]:
        return iter(())  # placeholder kept for API symmetry with async client

class AsyncRconClient:
    """Asyncio RCON client used by the Discord bot.

    Drop-in for :class:`RconClient` wherever async is preferred (e.g., inside
    a discord.py event loop to avoid blocking).
    """

    def __init__(self, host: str, port: int, password: str, timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT):
        self.host = host
        self.port = int(port)
        self.password = password
        self.timeout = timeout
        self._reader: asyncio.StreamReader | None = None
        self._writer: asyncio.StreamWriter | None = None
        self._id = 0

    async def connect(self) -> None:
        self._reader, self._writer = await asyncio.open_connection(self.host, self.port)
        self._id = 1
        await self._auth()

    async def _auth(self) -> None:
        if self._writer is None:
            raise RconError("not connected")
        self._writer.write(_encode(self._id, SERVERDATA_AUTH, self.password))
        await self._writer.drain()
        pkt = await self._read_packet()
        if pkt.request_id == -1:
            raise RconAuthError("RCON auth failed (bad password?)")

    async def send(self, command: str) -> str:
        if self._writer is None:
            await self.connect()
        assert self._writer is not None
        self._id += 1
        myid = self._id
        self._writer.write(_encode(myid, SERVERDATA_EXECCOMMAND, command))
        await self._writer.drain()
        out: list[bytes] = []
        while True:
            pkt = await self._read_packet()
            if pkt.ptype == SERVERDATA_RESPONSE and not pkt.body:
                break
            if pkt.body:
                out.append(pkt.body)
        return b"".join(out).decode("utf-8", "replace")

    async def _read_packet(self) -> RCONResponse:
        if self._reader is None:
            raise RconError("not connected")
        head = await self._reader.readexactly(4)
        size = struct.unpack("<i", head)[0]
        if size < 0 or size > 4096 * 16:
            raise RconError(f"invalid packet size: {size}")
        data = await self._reader.readexactly(size)
        pkt_id, ptype, body = _decode_header(head + data)
        return RCONResponse(pkt_id, ptype, bytes(body))

    async def send_many(self, commands: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:
        return [await self.send(c.strip()) for c in commands if c.strip()]

    async def close(self) -> None:
        if self._writer is not None:
            try:
                self._writer.close()
                await self._writer.wait_closed()
            finally:
                self._writer = None
                self._reader = None

    async def __aenter__(self) -> AsyncRconClient:
        await self.connect()
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
        await self.close()
